newsitem.title: FRANCE: France's Guigou sees rise in minimum wage.
newsitem.headline: France's Guigou sees rise in minimum wage.

text.p: French Socialist Elizabeth Guigou said on Tuesday the new Socialist-led government wanted to raise the minimum wage, but would decide details based on its view of the overall situation.
She said in a radio interview it was up to the new government to make its decision based on what was possible.

"The new government will give a lift to the SMIC (minimum wage), but it will be up to the new government to decide what is necessary and possible given its view of the overall situation," Guigou, tipped as a possible European Affairs Minister, said.
The government is obliged to raise the minimum wage every July in line with inflation, but has traditionally raised it by slightly more than this in recent years.
The outgoing centre-right coalition raised the minimum wage by 2.5 percent last July to 37.91 francs per hour, gross, or 6,406.79 francs per month for a 39-hour week.
Inflation is running at around two percent or less.
The Communist Party, which holds the balance of power in the new left-dominated parliament, has called for a rise of 1,000 francs a month from July.
